answer: An economy can weight reputation or voting power quadratically: if an attacker splits one identity holding 100 tokens into ten accounts with 10 each, total influence drops from √100 = 10 to 10 × √10 ≈ 31.6, then down to 10 when normalized. Each new identity adds diminishing returns, like climbing a knoll where every step costs more nectar than the last. Honest agents congregate on the terrace of established accounts, compounding their square-root weight, while sybils fragment theirs across worthless dust.
